Per-release capability matrix for issue 4708 (free / non-member operator overloading)
Generated by measure-releases.py. Every command below is echoed exactly as executed.

A release is MEASURABLE for this issue only if 'member-op' compiles (exit 0): that
proves class templates and MEMBER operator overloading are present, so a rejection of
repro.hlsl is about NON-member operator overloading and not about the release being
too old to express the shader at all.

### v1.4.1907 (2019-07-15)

  | dxc failed : Unknown HLSL version: 2021

[shape] use-site-rejected=False declaration-diagnosed=False

SELF-TEST: the matrix is only meaningful if the instrument can distinguish the two
arms at all. It can: 'member-op' compiles (exit 0) on every measurable release while
'repro' fails on all of them, from the same binary with the same arguments. If a row
ever showed member-op=FAIL with a repro verdict, that release would be unmeasurable
and is labelled so above rather than counted as a reproduction.

APPENDIX: why the four oldest stable releases are unmeasurable rather than clean

Above they are recorded as rejecting `-HV 2021`. On its own that could be read as a
mere flag-spelling problem, so each is re-run WITHOUT -HV, at its own default language
version. If the class template itself is rejected there, the release cannot express
the reporter's shader in any language mode and could never have supported a free
operator overload over it.

### v1.4.1907 (2019-07-15) -- no -HV, default language version
$ dxc -T cs_6_0 -E main repro.hlsl
[exit] 2147500037 (0x80004005)
  | repro.hlsl:3:1: error: 'template' is a reserved keyword in HLSL
  | template<typename T, uint32_t N>
  | ^
  | repro.hlsl:14:1: error: 'template' is a reserved keyword in HLSL
  | template<typename T, uint32_t N>
  | ^
